t: A land of the Bohemian crown with its own estates, diet and law, ruled from Olomouc and later Brno from 1182 to 1918.
Its religious tolerance sheltered the Unity of the Brethren, who printed the Kralice Bible, and Anabaptist Hutterite communities.
After 1620 the Habsburgs curbed its estates; it ended as a crown land of Austria-Hungary and joined Czechoslovakia in 1918.
dyk: The worldwide Moravian Church takes its name from Brethren refugees who left Moravia for Herrnhut in Saxony in 1722; its missionaries reached the Caribbean by 1732.
ev: Frederick Barbarossa makes Conrad III Otto of Znojmo margrave of Moravia
Charles IV grants Moravia to his brother John Henry, founding a Moravian Luxembourg line
Margrave Jobst of Moravia is elected King of the Romans
The Peace of Olomouc leaves Moravia to Matthias Corvinus of Hungary for his lifetime
The Unity of the Brethren begins printing the Kralice Bible
The Renewed Land Ordinance makes the crown hereditary and curbs the Moravian estates
Gregor Mendel publishes his plant experiments made in Brno
Moravia becomes a land of the new Czechoslovakia

f.capital: Olomouc and Brno; Brno from the 1640s
f.predecessor: Přemyslid appanage principalities of Olomouc, Brno and Znojmo
